cache removal on unmount is client code; the static host's index.html no-store and immutable hashed chunks (web/nginx.conf) already guarantee a fresh shell per load — nothing to provision
render-then-re-read is client code with server enforcement unchanged; no infrastructure
the 15 s deadline lives in client.ts (AbortController) and is covered by the console suite (cicd-pipeline.md stage 8); no infrastructure

the 20/min budget set on the existing PUT /v1/admin/users/{userId}/role entry in the gateway Route table over the existing Identity use case (infrastructure-specification.md 'What must exist'); its latency is an unmeasured target — status counters only until a latency histogram exists (monitoring-design.md fact 3)

two new gateway route entries (POST …/disable, POST …/restore) plus the /v1 registration of Identity's existing use cases (infrastructure-specification.md 'What must exist'); no stack change. Either path answers 405 where a use case is missing rather than promising a mutation

GET /v1/support-grants entry + Identity's SupportGrantRepository::list_by_status under its own DSN, with U3's required status index (infrastructure-specification.md Shared Infrastructure); Identity counts it under route="support.grants" but no latency series exists, so the p95 is unmeasured and ungated (monitoring-design.md)
approve/revoke ride the existing grant routes and handlers, unchanged; the reused queue adds no infrastructure
retry: false is a client query/mutation option; no retry exists in the gateway or Identity for these paths — nothing to provision

the per-route max_requests_per_minute on the gateway Route entries (set on the existing role-change entry, declared on the other four) is what produces the 429 with Retry-After (security-design §3); client rendering is code — no stack configuration
refetchOnWindowFocus/refetchInterval are client query options; no polling infrastructure exists for these reads

existing TLS edge unchanged: gateway published 443, web published 80, console data calls same-origin under the unchanged CSP connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co (infrastructure-specification.md Networking rows); no new browser-external origin
memory-only session and cache are code properties; the static host is read_only with tmpfs (existing) and stores nothing feature-side

20/min per-token budgets on the role/disable/restore Route entries — set on the existing PUT …/role declaration, since the table is first-match and a duplicate entry would be shadowed (gateway code, no stack change); the limiter is in-process per replica, so the fleet ceiling is that budget per gateway replica — stated in security-design §3
the rendered allowlist is a DTO/client property; no infrastructure holds or filters those fields
the unit writes no audit record; the lookup's and mutations' audit rows are Identity's server-side records (C9) on the existing path

the one added read runs on Identity's own Postgres role and DSN against U3's table — no schema, no privilege change; the required status index is U3's migration (infrastructure-specification.md 'What must exist')

role freshness is a provider read (RoleReader::read_role) on the existing Supabase Auth adapter: connect 1 s / total 3 s / one attempt, failure → 503; no new credential, service or origin (infrastructure-specification.md Infrastructure Services)
ARIA structure and focus handling are client code, verified by the console suite (cicd-pipeline.md stage 8)
Intl.DateTimeFormat and the role/status word mapping are client code; the console bundle is built into the existing web image — no infrastructure

D-S1's body-carrying POST keeps the looked-up address out of every logged URL, and the address is never in a header; the edge log format is unchanged (infrastructure-specification.md Shared Infrastructure 'Edge access logs'). Reasons travel in bodies
memory-only drafts and the unmount cache removal are client code; the static host's read_only/tmpfs configuration (existing) means nothing reaches disk
the absence of JWT decode/validation in the console is a code property; no infrastructure

all five paths declared requires_admin: true in the gateway's deny-by-default Route table (infrastructure-specification.md Shared Infrastructure) and re-checked in Identity from the forwarded JWT — undeclared paths 404 before a service is reached
presentational gating plus the same five route entries: a support session that opens the section is refused 403 by the gateway/Identity, not by the console — server enforcement is the routed surface

the gateway's existing per-token check_route limiter, in-process per replica (2 replicas in infra/swarm-stack.yml); no configuration change, and the per-replica bound is stated rather than presented as global. A 429 has no metric of its own — only the edge access log shows it (monitoring-design.md 429 row)

status + correlation id rendering is client code; the x-correlation-id header is the gateway's existing facility
React default escaping is a code property; no infrastructure
